title: Downhole survey station
description:
Azimuth and dip measured at a depth down a hole. The stations are what bend a hole away from its collar orientation.

GENERATED from the normative OpenAPI document (`spec/openapi.yaml`) — do not edit by hand; run `python scripts/regenerate.py`. The OpenAPI document is normative for the wire; this file is the same contract for one record type, readable on its own.

bhid.description: Natural key of the drill hole: `{"hole_id", "project", "company"}`.

depth_at.description: Depth of this measurement ALONG the hole from the collar, in `length_units` — not a vertical depth, and not a distance from surface once the hole deviates.

display_units.description: Units the *_display strings on this record are formatted in, from the project's display preference. Presentation only: the stored values remain in `length_units`.

azimuth.description: Azimuth in DEGREES, clockwise from grid north (0–360). On a collar it is the orientation the hole was set up to drill; on a downhole survey station it is the measured orientation at that depth.

dip.description: Dip in DEGREES from horizontal. ⚠️ NEGATIVE IS DOWNWARD: a vertical hole drilled straight down is -90, a horizontal hole is 0. On a collar it is the set-up inclination; on a survey station it is the measured inclination at that depth.

project_id.description: The project this record is in (a credential may read several; GET /api/v2/grant-context/ names them).

items.description: What is wrong with a stored row. geoDB returns stored data as it is; this marks it so it can be found and corrected.

code.description: `azimuth_out_of_range`: azimuth (or dip direction) is outside 0..360 degrees.; `coordinate_outside_crs`: the coordinate cannot be in its epsg (degrees beyond ±90 latitude or ±180 longitude under EPSG:4326).; `crs_implausible`: the coordinate looks like degrees of longitude/latitude but its epsg is a projected system in metres or feet, so it sits near that grid's origin (often at the equator on a map).; `depth_past_hole`: the depth lies beyond the hole's total depth.; `dip_out_of_range`: dip is outside -90..90 degrees.; `interval_upside_down`: depth_from is greater than depth_to (an upside-down interval).; `invalid_geometry`: the stored geometry is not valid (for example a self-intersecting outline).; `missing_epsg`: the record has coordinates but no epsg, so their CRS is unknown.; `negative_value`: a depth, length or total depth is negative.; `sample_trashed`: the assay's sample is in the trash; the assay is kept (never deleted with its sample) and re-links if the sample is restored or re-imported — leave it out of statistics unless told otherwise.

data_warnings.description: Present only when this stored row has a problem geoDB can recognise (an upside-down interval, a dip past 90°, coordinates with no CRS…). The row is returned exactly as stored — never fixed or hidden; correct it with an update.
